title: devlab flash's first real flash
done: The pristine stock Sxmo image flashed to surya with devlab flash: fixes baked in, device tree a43d069d0a49adcd, the phone booted and passed all 20 checks. Two things done by hand after it became the tool's job: a fresh phone's clock is at its image's build date (certificates looked invalid) and its first boot grew the partition but left the filesystem at 2 GB - devlab provision now sets the clock and grows the system first.
considered: Leaving both as notes for whoever flashes next.
rejected: That: what must be known to use a tool belongs in the tool.

title: It tells its essence
done: Its idea written for anyone, and its workings: what delivers and proves each step of its path, and why we care. Steps that nothing serves yet are left empty, to be seen.
rejected: That: a step nothing serves is a wish, and should show.

title: The ear in health
done: devlab health --hear listens as part of health: heard checks join the one baseline and regress like any other. The rule made honest rather than a second baseline: a run that did not listen is out of scope for what only listening tells. The watcher never makes a sound by itself.
considered: Listening after every start; a separate baseline for heard checks.
rejected: The first: a tone in the night. The second: two truths about one phone.

title: What the ear heard is withdrawn
done: The microphone was the author's earphones, worn on his head: its distance from the phone changed as he moved. The levels measured, the difference seen between the two speakers, and the passes themselves cannot be relied on. The heard checks are out of the baseline and the lab's microphone is un-named until one is fixed in place; the tool stays, proven to work mechanically.
considered: Keeping the results with a caveat.
rejected: That: evidence from an instrument that moves is not evidence, and a later failure would have looked like the phone getting worse.

title: The lab's ear
done: devlab hear joins what existed - the tone tool, the lab's microphone, the phone's player: the room recorded in silence, a tone played on each channel at a known volume and recorded, measured against the noise around it and the silent room. Both of surya's speakers heard on the first run. For any phone: its lab names a microphone, its manifest names the tones.
considered: Trusting that a loaded driver and an unmuted control mean sound.
rejected: That: a machine should hear it. And claiming which speaker is which - one microphone cannot tell.
